name: ash-vscode
description: Runs the ASH CLI over the open workspace and reports its SARIF findings as editor diagnostics. Ships no scanners and no copy of ASH.

untrustedWorkspaces.description: A scan runs ASH over the workspace, and ASH reads the workspace's own .ash/.ash.yaml, which can load Python plugin modules and so run code the repository supplies. Trust the workspace to scan it.

ash.executablePath.markdownDescription:
The ASH executable to run. Empty (the default) runs `ashx` from PATH, and runs `ash` instead when `ashx` is not installed, with a one-time notice. Any other value is run exactly as given, with no fallback. On Windows with MSYS2 or Git Bash on PATH, a bare `ash` can resolve to the Almquist shell instead of ASH; set this to `automated-security-helper`, which ASH installs as a permanent alias for exactly that case.

Machine-scoped: this names a program that gets executed, so a cloned repository cannot set it from its own `.vscode/settings.json`.

ash.outputDirectory.markdownDescription:
Directory the scan writes to, relative to the workspace folder. ASH writes its SARIF report to `reports/ash.sarif` underneath it.

It must resolve, symlinks included, to a folder inside the workspace folder. ASH clears directories under it before each scan, so an absolute path, a `..` escape or a link out of the workspace is refused and nothing runs.

ash.extraArguments.markdownDescription: Extra arguments appended to `ashx scan`, for example `--scanners detect-secrets` or `--offline`. `--output-dir` and `--source-dir` are refused, in either form: the extension sets both, and `ash.outputDirectory` chooses where the scan writes.

ash.scanTimeoutSeconds.markdownDescription: Seconds to wait for a scan before stopping it and every process it started. `0` waits indefinitely. A scan can also be stopped from its progress notification.

scripts.test:integration: npm run compile && npm run compile:integration && node out-integration/test/integration/run.js
